words: قُلْ يُحْيِيهَا ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنشَأَهَآ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most deniers offer no proof and rely on sheer improbability, as in their questions about being raised after becoming dust or bones.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن المنكرين للحشر منهم من لم يذكر فيه دليلا ولا شبهة بل اكتفى بمجرد الاستبعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rebuts their incredulity by recalling that He first formed humans from dust and semen, fashioned diverse organs, and gave them speech and intellect, the grounds of their honor.
rows.anchor: نسي أنا خلقناه من تراب ثم من نطفة متشابهة الأجزاء ثم جعلنا له من ناصيته إلى قدمه أعضاء مختلفة الصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If deniers find original creation of a speaking, reasoning person from a filthy, lifeless drop plausible, they have no basis to find restoration implausible.
rows.anchor: فإن كانوا يقنعون بمجرد الاستبعاد فهلا يستبعدون خلق الناطق العاقل من نطفة قذرة لم تكن محلا للحياة أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One objection says that after annihilation nothing remains, so existence cannot be predicated of what is nonexistent; God answers that He can restore people as He first created them when they were unremembered.
rows.anchor: أنه بعد العدم لم يبق شيئا فكيف يصح على العدم الحكم بالوجود فأجاب تعالى عن هذه الشبهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second objection asks how dispersed bodily parts, including parts eaten by animals or incorporated into another person's body, can be reunited without depriving either person of a body.
rows.anchor: أن من تفرقت أجزاؤه في مشارق العالم ومغاربه وصار بعضه في أبدان السباع وبعضه في حواصل الطيور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's complete knowledge of every creation refutes the difficulty of distinguishing the dispersed parts needed for resurrection.
rows.anchor: فأبطل الله هذه الشبهة بقوله : {وهو بكل خلق عليم}

rows.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
rows.claim: A learned authority frames the problem as both intermingled body parts and the dryness of decayed bones, since life requires bodily moisture.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الأفاضل : لما كان تمسكهم بكون العظام رميمة من وجهين : أحدهما : اختلاط أجزاء الأبدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge enables Him to distinguish the parts of different bodies, answering the first difficulty.
rows.anchor: أشار إلى جواب الأول بقوله : {وهو بكل خلق عليم} فيمكنه تمييز أجزاء الأبدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The green tree that yields fire answers the second difficulty: God can restore freshness to what has become dry and decayed.
rows.anchor: وإلى جواب الثاني بقوله : {الذى جعل لكم من الشجر الاخضر نارا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A tree is a plant with a trunk; green lies between white and black and leans toward black, so black can also be called green.
rows.anchor: ماله ساق والخضرة أحد الألوان بين البياض والسواد وهو إلى السواد أقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjective is masculine because شجر is grammatically masculine, although its collective sense as a group of trees is feminine; Iraq's blackness is also associated with its abundant greenery.
rows.anchor: ووصف الشجر بالأخضر دون الخضراء نظرا إلى اللفظ فإن لفظ الشجر مذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For human benefit God makes fire from green trees such as marakh and afar; marakh catches fire quickly, while afar is another fire-producing tree.
rows.anchor: والمعنى خلق لأجلكم ومنفعتكم من الشجر الأخضر كالمرخ والعفار

rows.speaker: الحكماء
rows.claim: The sages say every tree contains fire except the jujube; dyers use it to beat cloth, and Arabs make fire sticks from marakh and afar.
rows.anchor: قال الحكماء : لكل شجر نار إلا العناب فمن ذلك يدق القصار الثوب عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rubbing two still-green sticks, marakh as the male against afar as the female, produces fire by God's permission even though both drip with water.
rows.anchor: يقطع الرجل منهما غصنين كالسواكين وهما أخضران يقطر منهما الماء فيسحق المرخ وهو ذكر على العفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle إذا marks suddenness, the prepositional phrase attaches to توقدون, and its pronoun refers to the tree; الإيقاد means kindling fire.
rows.anchor: إذا للمفاجأة والجار متعلق بتوقدون والضمير راجع إلى الشجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People readily accept fire from green wood, so they should accept resurrection; producing fire from watery wood shows God's power to unite opposites and restore what dried out.
rows.anchor: كذلك لا تشكون في أن الله يحيي الموتى ويخرجهم من القبور للسؤال والجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccan disbelievers rejected the arrival of a warner from their own people as outside possibility, seeing Muhammad as their equal in appearance, character, lineage, and social standing; they failed to wonder at their carved idols.
rows.anchor: عجب كفار أهل مكة من أن جاءهم منذر ينذرهم النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their inconsistent perplexity led them to accuse the Prophet of magic and lying.
rows.anchor: فلما تحيروا في شأن النبي عليه السلام نسبوه إلى السحر والكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit noun الكافرون replaces an expected pronoun to censure them and signal that only deeply immersed disbelievers would dare say this.
rows.anchor: وضع فيه الظاهر موضع المضمر غضبا عليهم وإيذانا بأنه لا يتجاسر على مثل ما يقولونه إلا المتوغلون في الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call the warner a magician for the wonders he displays and a great liar for claiming that God sent him revelation.
rows.anchor: فيما يظهره من الخوارق {كذاب}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intensive form كذّاب preserves the rhyme and suits their claim that his lies concern every Quranic verse, unlike the comparatively rare display of wonders; lying about God is especially grave.
rows.anchor: ولأن الكذب على الله ليس كالكذب على غيره ولكثرة الكذب في زعمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tawilat al-Najmiyya says diseased hearts, estranged from truth, interpreted prophethood as magic and the truthful Prophet as a liar according to their distorted understanding.
rows.anchor: لما كانوا منحرفي مزاج القلوب لمرض نسيان الحق جاءت النبوة على مذاق عقولهم المتغيرة سحرا

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says blindness of judgment mistakes the lights of revelation for sorcery and cannot distinguish the rays of truth from the darkness of falsehood.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي (جه تيره رايي كه أنوار لمعات وحى را أزتاريكىء سحر امتياز نكند

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: The accompanying poem compares the denier to a bat that cannot perceive the sun, though its radiance illuminates the world.
rows.anchor: كشته طالع آفتابي أنيينين عالم فروز ديدة خفاش را يكذره ازوى نورته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recognition of prophethood and sainthood is easy for the divinely aided, whose hearts turn from everything besides God; those deprived of aid turn away from God and slander His prophets and saints.
rows.anchor: فإن قلوبهم ألفت الإعراض عن الله

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Junayd says affirming the mystics' knowledge counts as the lesser sainthood, distinct from the greater sainthood.
rows.anchor: قال الأستاذ أبو القاسم الجنيد رضي الله عنه التصديق بعلمنا هذا ولاية

rows.speaker: اليافعي
rows.claim: Yafi'i divides people into four grades: belief, knowledge, and taste; belief and knowledge without taste; belief alone; and none of the three, the last group slandering spiritual elect through estrangement from their way.
rows.anchor: قال اليافعي : والناس على أربعة أقسام : القسم الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: انطلق means to go away; الملأ means the chiefs rather than any crowd, named for filling eyes with their prestige and hearts with awe.
rows.anchor: الانطلاق الذهاب والملأ الأشراف لا مطلق الجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Twenty-five Quraysh leaders left Abu Talib's gathering after the Prophet silenced them, saw his resolve to prevail in religion, and gave up hope of a compromise through Abu Talib.
rows.anchor: وذهب الأشراف من قريش وهم خمسة وعشرون عن مجلس أبي طالب بعد ما أسكتهم رسول الله عليه السلام بالجواب الحاضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle أن explains the implied speech in their departure: leaving a council where they had conversed necessarily involved speech, here advice among themselves.
rows.anchor: مفسرة للمقول المدلول عليه بالانطلاق لأن الانطلاق عن مجلس التقاول لا يخلو عن القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their instruction امشوا means to follow your own way and leave, since there is no benefit in remaining where this man is.
rows.anchor: سيروا على طريقتكم وامضوا فلا فائدة في مكانة هذا الرجل

rows.speaker: المهدوي
rows.claim: Al-Mahdawi reports that Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt was the one who said امشوا.
rows.anchor: وحكى المهدوي أن قائلها عقبة بن أبي معيط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs tell one another to remain in worship of their gods and endure the criticism they hear about them.
rows.anchor: واثبتوا على عبادتها متحملين لما تسمعونه في حقها من القدح

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: If unbelievers urge one another to persist with idols, believers have still greater reason for steadfast worship and sincere lovers for patience in seeking the Beloved.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى أن الكفار إذا تراضوا فيما بينهم بالصبر على آلهتهم فالمؤمنون أولى بالصبر على عبادة معبودهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause إن هذا لشيء يراد either explains their command to be patient or gives the reason they must obey it.
rows.anchor: تعليل للأمر بالصبر أو لوجوب الامتثال به

rows.speaker: أبو السعود
rows.claim: Abu al-Su'ud reads it as Muhammad's determined plan to establish monotheism and abolish their idols, not a passing remark or a matter to be softened by Abu Talib's intercession.
rows.anchor: ما ذهب إليه المولى أبو السعود في "الإرشاد"

rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: Al-Jalalayn takes the phrase to mean a plot aimed at them and a scheme being made against them.
rows.anchor: لأمر يراد بنا ومكر يمكر علينا

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: Sa'di al-Mufti suggests it may mean that their religion is worthy of being sought and firmly held, encouraging the preceding command to patience.
rows.anchor: وقال سعدي المفتي : وسنح بالبال أنه يجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation says Muhammad's opposition and the events threatening them are decreed and unavoidable.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : (بدرستى كه مخالفت محمد باما جيز نيست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi proposes that they mean patience in the old religion is required of them and is their strongest defense against Muhammad's mission, as they expect death to overtake him.
rows.anchor: أن الصبر والثبات على عبادة الآلهة التي هي الدين القديم يراد منكم فإنه أقوى ما يدفع به أمر محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they may regard Muhammad's rising as a danger that must be extinguished before it spreads and prevails.
rows.anchor: أو أن شأن محمد لشيء يراد دفعه وإطفاء نائرته بأي وجه كان قبل أن يعلو ويشيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their repeated gathering to plot against the Prophet shows that they intended harm, but God insisted on bringing His light to completion.
rows.anchor: ودل عليه اجتماعهم على مكره عليه السلام مرارا فأبى الله إلا أن يتم نوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By this they mean the Prophet's teaching of God's oneness.
rows.anchor: ما سمعنا بهاذا} : الذي يقوله من التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is an adverbial attached to سمعنا and means the religion in which they found their forefathers, the Quraysh tradition that came later than previous religions.
rows.anchor: ظرف لغو سمعنا ؛ أي : في الملة التي أدركنا عليها آباءنا

words: مَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَٰذَا فِى ٱلْمِلَّةِ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their appeal to inherited religion signals the ignorant reliance on custom and imitation of ancestral error instead of a sound path of worship.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى ركون الجهال إلى التقليد والعادة وما وجدوا عليه أسلافهم من الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited Persian verse warns that a traveler may follow a route believing it leads to the Kaaba when it actually leads to Turkistan.
rows.anchor: ترسم نرسى بكعبه اي اعرابى كين ره كه توميروى بتركستانست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Milla, like din, properly means the law God prescribed through prophets so servants may attain His reward and nearness; applying it to polytheist custom is figurative by analogy.
rows.anchor: والملة كالدين اسم لما شرع الله لعباده على يد الأنبياء ليتوصلوا به إلى ثواب الله وجواره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here إن is a negator equivalent to ما; اختلاق means a lie invented by the speaker himself.
rows.anchor: إن هاذآ} : نافية بمعنى ما {إلا اختلاق}

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says that when خلق describes speech, it means a lie; some therefore avoided applying the term خلق to the Quran.
rows.anchor: في "المفردات" : وكل موضع استعمل فيه الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They object that revelation came to Muhammad though they were the leaders, nobility, elders, wealthiest, and best supported, and deny that the Quran is a reminder sent from God.
rows.anchor: ونحن رؤساء الناس وأشرافهم وأكبرهم سنا وأكثرهم أموالا وأعوانا وأحقاء بكل منصب شريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claims reveal envy that the Prophet alone was granted prophethood and a fixation on worldly status; real honor lies in inward virtues, not outward advantages.
rows.anchor: دليل على أن مناط تكذيبهم ليس إلا الحسد على اختصاصه عليه السلام بشرف النبوة من بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Comparing Muhammad to themselves is a false analogy: he is the spirit of spirits and origin of creation, while human form is a common inheritance from Adam; his face nevertheless shone with unequalled beauty.
rows.anchor: فلأن قياس نفسه عليه السلام بأنفسهم فاسد إذ هو روح الأرواح وأصل الخليقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi applies the verse to contemporary scholars and worshippers who deny a God-knowing master revealing truths they neither understand nor have tasted, instead of benefiting from his presence and light.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى حال أكثر علماء زماننا وعبادهم أنهم إذا رأوا عالما ربانيا من أرباب الحقائق

words: بَلْ هُم فِى شَكٍّۢ مِّن ذِكْرِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their rebellious egos ask why this knower was chosen from among them, reject his teaching, and lapse into doubt.
rows.anchor: فيجحدونه بدل الاغتنام بأنفاسه والاقتباس من أنواره

words: بَلْ هُم فِى شَكٍّۢ مِّن ذِكْرِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remembrance in which they doubt is the Quran or revelation; their imitation and refusal to examine evidence leave them unsettled, alternating between accusations of magic and fabrication.
rows.anchor: أي : القرآن أو الوحي بميلهم إلى التقليد وإعراضهم عن النظر في الأدلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza is interrogative and condemnatory, the fa links to an omitted clause, and man is either conditional or relative with an elided predicate indicated by what follows.
rows.anchor: للاستفهام الإنكاري ، والفاء : للعطف على محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: شرح originally means spreading or opening meat; opening the breast is by divine light, tranquility, and a spirit from God.
rows.anchor: ومنه شرح الصدر بنور إلهي وسكينة من جهته تعالى وروح منه

rows.speaker: أبو السعود
rows.claim: Abu al-Su'ud defines expansion for Islam as completing one's readiness for it: the chest houses the heart, source of the spirit linked to the soul that accepts Islam, and its expansion widens and illumines the heart before Islam.
rows.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" : شرح الصدر للإسلام عبارة عن تكميل الاستعداد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi frames the contrast as whether all people are equal, introducing the distinction between the one given an open breast and others.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : أكل الناس سواء فمن بالفارسية : (بس هركسى ويا آنكس كه).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the person broad-chested and ready for Islam; he remained on original human disposition without acquired distortions.
rows.anchor: أي : خلقه متسع الصدر مستعدا للإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The open-hearted person rests in great divine light: God's favor enables him to recognize and follow the truth in cosmic and revealed signs, unlike those who darken their hearts by choice and ignore them.
rows.anchor: بموجب ذلك مستقر {على نور} عظيم {من ربه}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast recalls the person whose breast God makes constricted and closed, as in 6:125; light and darkness, like knowledge and ignorance, are not equal.
rows.anchor: يعني : ليس من هو على نور كمن هو على ظلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Muslim's light and happiness depend on knowledge and gnosis; each believer's distinctive gnosis determines the degree of spiritual rank.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه لا نور ولا سعادة لمسلم إلا بالعلم والمعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith and gnosis are lights of unequal reach: common believers resemble candlelight or a lamp, the truthful resemble moon and stars, and prophets the sun or more, revealing different expanses of the unseen realm.
rows.anchor: فإيمان آحاد العوام نوره كنور الشمع وبعضهم نوره كنور السراج وإيمان الصديقين نوره كنور القمر والنجوم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A prophetic report says people will be brought out of Hell according to measures of faith from half or quarter of a grain down to an atom, showing that faith's grades and their lights differ at the Resurrection, especially on the Bridge.
rows.anchor: ولهذا جاء في الحديث : "إنه يقال يوم القيامة أخرجوا من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وَيْل means severe punishment.
rows.anchor: فويل} (بس شدت عذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hardness is a thickening of the heart, named by analogy with hard stone; muqāsāt is the process of bearing or treating hardship.
rows.anchor: القسوة غلظ القلب وأصله من حجر قاس والمقاساة معالجة ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من can indicate cause or explanation: because of God's remembrance, which should open breasts and reassure hearts, they recoil and harden further when God and His signs are recalled.
rows.anchor: ومن أجلية وسببية كما في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their worsening hardness is compared to the increase of impurity in 9:125.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى : {فزادتهم رجسا} (التوبة : 125)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with عن instead of من means that their hearts are hardened against accepting God's remembrance.
rows.anchor: وقرىء عن ذكر الله ؛ أي : فويل للذين غلظت قلوبهم

rows.speaker: مالك بن دينار
rows.claim: Malik ibn Dinar says no punishment strikes a servant worse than a hardened heart, and God removes mercy from a people only when angry with them.
rows.anchor: وعن مالك بن دينار رحمه الله ما ضرب عبد بعقوبة أعظم من قسوة قلبه

rows.speaker: الله
rows.claim: In a private address to Moses, God warns that prolonged worldly hopes harden the heart, which then becomes distant from Him; Moses should wear worn clothes but keep a renewed heart.
rows.anchor: وقال الله تعالى لموسى عليه السلام في مناجاته يا موسى : لا تطل في الدنيا أملك

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith identifies love of food, sleep, and ease as three causes of hardness in the heart.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "تورث القسوة في القلب ثلاث خصال

rows.speaker: عائشة الصديقة
rows.claim: Al-Kashf al-Asrar says hardness grows from many sins and quotes Aisha that the first innovation after the Prophet was satiety; Dhun-Nun says a full meal brought him sin, while hunger let Shibli find fresh wisdom and lessons.
rows.anchor: وفي "كشف الأسرار" : (بدانكه ابن قسوة دل از بسيارى معصيت خيزد عائشة صديقه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith praises prolonged hunger and reflection, condemns gluttony, drinking, and much sleep, and recommends eating and drinking to half-full as part of prophecy.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "أفضلكم عند الله أطولكم جوعا وتفكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi quotes Sa'di's poem advising moderate eating, likening the human stomach to a vessel for food and remembrance rather than an empty space for appetite alone.
rows.anchor: باندازه خورزاد اكر آدمى جنين برشكم آدمى يا خمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those far from God, whose hearts have hardened, are in manifest misguidance obvious even to a minimally perceptive observer.
rows.anchor: البعداء الموصوفون بما ذكر من قساوة القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse applies generally to anyone whose breast God opens by creating faith within.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الآية عامة فيمن شرح صدره للإسلام بخلق الإيمان فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the verse was revealed about Hamza and Ali, whose breasts were opened to Islam, and Abu Lahab and his son, whose hearts hardened.
rows.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في حمزة بن عبد المطلب وعلي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنهما وأبي لهب

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In a report about the verse's revelation, the Prophet explains that divine light entering the heart expands it; its signs are turning to the eternal home, renouncing the delusive world, and preparing for death before it arrives.
rows.anchor: روي في الخبر أنه لما نزلت هذه الآية ، قالوا : كيف ذلك يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Faith is a light illuminating the heart's lamp and Islam its ray in the breast's niche; an expanded breast lives by the light of the Lord's care.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى أن الإيمان نور ينور الله به مصباح قلوب عباده المؤمنين والإسلام ضوء نور الإيمان

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Signs of this light include erasing blameworthy worldly desires, cultivating love of the Hereafter, good deeds and noble character; God erases and confirms as He wills, as 13:39 says.
rows.anchor: ومن أمارات ذلك النور محو آثار ظلمات الصفات الذميمة النفسانية من حب الدنيا وزينتها وشهواتها

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Another sign is that remembrance softens the heart and deepens longing for God, making the seeker weary of worldly trials and bestial, predatory, and satanic traits so that he flees to God.
rows.anchor: ومن أماراته أن تلين قلوبهم لذكر الله فتزداد أشواقهم إلى لقاء الله تعالى وجواره

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The way proceeds through lights of knowledge, understanding, certainty, manifestation of the attributes, witnessing of the essence, and the majesty of divine oneness, until ordinary notions of self, aim, nearness, and separation fall away.
rows.anchor: نور المشاهدة بظهور الذات ثم أنوار جلال الصمدية بحقائق التوحيد

rows.speaker: جامي
rows.claim: Jami's poem counsels the seeker not to dwell on nearness, distance, union, or separation after transcending such distinctions.
rows.anchor: جامى مكن انديشه زنز ديكى ودورى لا قرب ولا بعد ولا وصل ولا بين

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti calls expansion's light a great gift borne only by those upheld with divine care: care protects bodily forms, while providence protects spiritual realities.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي : نور الشرح منحة عظيمة

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Al-Kashf al-Asrar maps four inner layers: breast as the seat of Islam's covenant, heart as faith's light, fu'ad as the secret of witnessing, and shighaf as the station of love, with Quranic parallels at 2:22, 53:11, and 12:30.
rows.anchor: وفي "كشف الأسرار" : (بدان كه دل آدمى را جهارا برده است. برده أول صدر

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: God first clears the breast of whims and innovations and sets it on the Sunnah, then purifies the heart of worldly attachment and blameworthy traits, opens knowledge and wisdom in the fu'ad, and leads the shighaf from clay toward annihilation.
rows.anchor: اول نظرى كند بصد روى تاسينه وى از هوى وبدعتها باك كردد وقدم وى برجاده سنت مستقيم شود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author adopts a three-part account of light: the tongue's light is testimony to oneness, the body's is service and obedience, and the heart's is longing and love; they lead respectively to Paradise, Firdaws, and beholding the Beloved, with verses 5:85, 18:107, and 75:22-23 as proofs.
rows.anchor: نور زبان توحيد است وشهادت. ونورتن خدمت است وطاعت.

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith warns that people blessed with divine favors have enemies and should beware of them.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إن لأهل النعم أعداء فاحذروهم"
